result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as mock resources, and the two new tests pass along with the existing `SourceFileFilterTest`.

- **`ScopingConventions.java`** (`addTestConventions`): I replaced the two folder rules `.*/__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` and `.*/mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` with one rule, `.*/(__)?mock[^/]*/.*`. The `[^/]*` lets the rest of the folder name be anything except a slash, so `mock`, `mock.data`, `mock(old)`, `mock-größe` and `mock模拟` all match. The leading `/` and trailing `/` keep the match inside one folder name, so `remock/` and `mock.java` or `mockery.java` files don't match. The `_mock.*` file rule and the existing `mockapi`/`mocks` rules are unchanged.
- **`ScopingConventionsTest.java`** (new, under `codeanalyzer/src/test/.../scoping/`): checks the mock-folder convention against the positive cases (including backslash paths and every folder listed in the task), and the negative cases (`remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, `mock.java`, `mockery.java`).

Nothing is committed. A folder named `mockery/` now also counts as mock resources, since the task says any folder starting with `mock`.
